A.note: The target painting shown unchanged inside a flat brown border, slightly scaled down. The character and painting are intact. Only the added frame and the reduced scale differ.

B.note: Square dark vignette with an added soft halo. The flame crown is smoother and blobbier, and the fine wisps and the top-right swirl are reduced. The original warm brown background is mostly replaced by black.

C.note: A smooth 3D render: an egg-shaped head, glossy eyes with specular highlights, a radial fringe of uniform flame ribbons, stick legs and no tail. It is a different character in a different medium.

D.note: Appears identical to B: a square vignette with a halo, smoothed flames, lost wisps and a background replaced by black.

E.note: Appears identical to B and D: a square vignette with smoothed flame detail and an added halo glow.

F.note: A round vignette that keeps the painted wisps and the swirl, with the character slightly reduced. The outer background is darkened to black, so the painted atmosphere is cut back.

G.note: The full painting, but heavily blurred or low resolution. The brushwork, the flame strands and the eye edges are lost. Composition and colour are kept.

H.note: Appears identical to F: a round vignette with detail retained and a darkened surround.

C.note: Appears identical to A: a square vignette with a halo glow, fewer sparks and a black surround.

D.note: Appears identical to A and C.

F.note: Appears identical to B: a round vignette with detail retained and a darkened surround.

G.note: The target painting unchanged inside a flat brown border, slightly scaled down.

H.note: The full painting, heavily blurred. The brushwork, the flame strands and the spark crispness are lost, and the eye highlights are soft.

A.note: Square vignette with an added hot halo around the head and the hand fireballs. The flames are slightly more saturated and smoothed, and fewer embers show. The painted background and ground glow are largely blacked out.

B.note: A round vignette that keeps the strands and embers, with the character slightly smaller. The surround is darkened and the painted backdrop is partly lost.

C.note: The target painting unchanged inside a flat brown border, slightly scaled down.

E.note: Appears identical to B: a round vignette with detail retained.

G.note: The full painting, heavily blurred. The brushwork and the fine flame strands are lost, and the brow and eye edges are softened.

A.note: The full painting, heavily blurred. The brushwork, the smoke strands and the fine embers are lost. It keeps the grey rectangular patch at bottom right that is present in the target.

B.note: Square dark vignette in which the rising smoke plume is almost entirely lost to black. The legs and body fade into darkness, and the whole scene is much darker than the painting. The grey patch is gone.

C.note: A round vignette with a tight radius. Part of the smoke plume shows faintly, and the background and lower body are darker than in the target. The grey patch is removed.

D.note: A round vignette with a wider radius that keeps most of the smoke plume, the embers and the painted texture. The surround is darkened to black, and the grey patch is hidden.

E.note: Appears identical to B: smoke mostly lost and a very dark presentation.

F.note: The target painting unchanged inside a flat brown border, slightly scaled down, including the grey patch at bottom right.

G.note: A 3D render: a wide mushroom-like dark head, tall bright flame ribbons and a cartoon grey smoke coil. The droopy eyes read as sad, but the character, the flame state and the medium are clearly different, and the flames are too large for 'depleted'.

H.note: Appears identical to D: a round wide vignette that keeps the smoke and embers, with a darkened surround.

general_notes: Each state has the same five presentation variants: (1) the target unchanged inside a flat brown border; (2) a heavily blurred copy of the full painting; (3) a round dark vignette that keeps most painted detail (two identical copies per state); (4) a square dark vignette with an added halo, smoother or lost fine flame and smoke detail and a much darker surround (two or three copies per state; in depleted these lose most of the smoke plume); (5) a stylised 3D render that is a different character. Within a group, the copies looked identical to me, but I could not compare them pixel by pixel, so tiny differences may exist. The depleted target has a flat grey rectangle at bottom right, which looks like a source artifact; I did not penalise variants that hide it. Scaling and minor smoothing in the vignette variants were judged only at the displayed resolution. Depleted C may be the same as D and H with a tighter vignette, or may be its own variant; I scored it a little lower because more of the smoke is lost.
